tasks.topic: ресеты полки: настоящий дедлайн категории — чужая дата
tasks.text:
A store reset starts at 5am. Two people, a planogram printout, and a cart of product that has to go somewhere.

I've watched brands lose their slot in that hour without anyone deciding anything against them. The facings moved because a new item needed room, and the brand that couldn't ship in time for the window simply wasn't there to defend itself.

The reset calendar is the real deadline in this category. Not the launch date, not the trade show, not the PO. Everything upstream - artwork approval, co-man line time, first production run - is a countdown to somebody else's date, and missing it by two weeks costs you six months.

What I've learned the hard way: work backwards from the reset, not forwards from your roadmap. If the window is March, the answer to "when do we lock artwork" is not "February".

How far out do you lock your dates before a reset?

tasks.topic: fill rate — маркетинговое число, а не операционное
tasks.text:
The most expensive mistake a small brand makes isn't a bad ad. It's a short shipment.

A hole on the shelf costs the retailer labour to fix, a lost sale, and a data point that says your item doesn't move. You get charged for the first part and blamed for the third. Your sell-through report looks soft, and nobody writes down why.

So we treat fill rate as a marketing number, not an ops number. It decides whether the buyer defends you at the next review - and buyers defend the brands that never make them explain a gap.

Sales gets you onto the shelf. Operations keeps you there. Different people, different skills, and most brands staff only the first one.

What's the fill rate where you start having the hard conversation - 95%? 90%?
